story.question: What does 7 % 3 return?
story.takeaway: For nonnegative integers and a positive divisor, % returns the remainder after full groups.

intro.title:
AFTER GROUPING.
WHAT REMAINS?
intro.vo: Split seven into groups of three. What does the percent sign in this code tell us?
intro.label: THE REMAINDER OPERATOR

scenes.title: FILL EACH GROUP.
scenes.vo: Start with seven dots. Put three into the first group, then three into the second group. One dot remains, too few to fill another group. So seven modulo three is one.

scenes.title: ADD ONE DOT.
scenes.vo: Keep the two groups and add one dot to make eight. The two dots outside still cannot fill a group of three. The remainder is now two.

scenes.title: AN EXACT FIT.
scenes.vo: Add one dot to make nine. The three remaining dots form a third group. Nothing remains outside, so the remainder is zero.

outro.title:
KEEP WHAT
REMAINS.
outro.vo: Here the percent sign gives the remainder, not the number of groups. An exact division leaves zero. This example uses nonnegative integers and a positive divisor.
